repository.name: @webex/internal-plugin-calendar
repository.purpose: Internal calendar plugin registered as webex.internal.calendar. It registers the device and Mercury and keeps an in-memory meeting collection current from Mercury calendar create, update, and delete events; lists and syncs meetings for a date window (fetching participants a listing omits); reads notes, participants, and scheduler data; creates, updates, and deletes calendar events with payloads encrypted under a KMS key it creates on first use; and runs free-busy lookups that are sent over HTTPS and answered over Mercury. Its inbound payload transformer decrypts meeting reads through the conversation plugin's decryptTextProp transform.

integration.framework: karma (webex-legacy-tools --integration --runner karma; runs the unit and integration specs in browsers)
external_deps: live Webex services (calendar, KMS, Mercury, device registration)

calendar-internal-sdk.summary: Published npm package (internal plugin; README says semver is not strictly followed). main is dist/index.js and devMain is src/index.js. Importing it imports the device, encryption, and conversation plugins and registers Calendar as internal plugin 'calendar' with the config in src/config.js and the inbound transformMeetingNotes, transformMeetingParticipants, transformMeetingArray, and transformMeeting payload transformers. The only export is the default Calendar class. The plugin API is webex.internal.calendar (register, unregister, syncCalendar, getAll, getByType, list, getNotes, getNotesByUrl, getParticipants, processMeetingEvent, createCalendarEvent, updateCalendarEvent, deleteCalendarEvent, getSchedulerData, getFreeBusy) and the events calendar:registered, calendar:unregistered, calendar:create, calendar:update, calendar:delete from src/constants.js. Per-method behavior is in src/docs/README.md.

calendar-service-http.source: Webex calendar service (catalog service 'calendar', plus the participantsUrl and notesUrl carried by meeting objects; route definitions are not in this repository)
calendar-service-http.summary: GET calendarEvents with fromDate and toDate, GET calendarEvents/<base64url id>/notes, GET participantsUrl and notesUrl, POST calendarEvents/sync, PATCH and DELETE calendarEvents/<base64url id>/sync, GET schedulerData with the QuerySchedulerDataOptions query, and POST freebusy. Bodies are listed under Protocol and wire format in src/docs/README.md.

mercury-calendar-events.source: Mercury events for calendar (Mercury service; envelope routing owned by @webex/internal-plugin-mercury, module spec consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-mercury/src/docs/README.md)
mercury-calendar-events.summary: Inbound calendar.meeting.create, calendar.meeting.create.minimal, calendar.meeting.update, calendar.meeting.update.minimal, and calendar.meeting.delete envelopes carry data.calendarMeetingExternal; calendar.free_busy carries data.calendarFreeBusyScheduleResponse {requestId, encryptionKeyUrl, calendarFreeBusyItems}.

webex-core-plugin-host.summary: Calendar extends WebexPlugin in namespace Calendar (config is webex.config.calendar); registerInternalPlugin merges config and concatenates payloadTransformer predicates and transforms; PayloadTransformerInterceptor runs the inbound transforms on every response; webex.transform runs them on demand; canAuthorize gates register; webex.request carries every HTTP call.

internal-plugin-mercury.source: @webex/internal-plugin-mercury (workspace package, not declared in package.json and registered through the encryption plugin import; module spec consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-mercury/src/docs/README.md)
internal-plugin-mercury.summary: connect() and disconnect() own the socket; inbound envelopes are emitted as event:<eventType>; on and off subscribe to the calendar events.

internal-plugin-device.summary: register() before Mercury connects (a registered device refreshes) and unregister() after Mercury disconnects.

internal-plugin-encryption.source: @webex/internal-plugin-encryption (workspace package; no spec exists; code consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-encryption/src/encryption.js, src/kms.js, src/index.js)
internal-plugin-encryption.summary: encryptText(key, plaintext) and decryptText(key, ciphertext) resolve JWE strings; kms.createUnboundKeys({count: 1}) resolves keys with uri. Importing it imports the mercury plugin.

internal-plugin-conversation.source: @webex/internal-plugin-conversation (workspace package; no spec exists; code consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-conversation/src/decryption-transforms.js, src/conversation.js, src/config.js)
internal-plugin-conversation.summary: Supplies the inbound decryptTextProp transform, appended on webex ready when conversation.includeDecryptionTransforms is true (default). A field that fails to decrypt is set to decryptionFailureMessage ('This message cannot be decrypted') and the transform resolves.
